review_notes: Reviewed all of MultipointOrdinaryProbability.lean (lines 1-51): `multipointConstant`, `multipointConstant_pos` and `RegularSLEPresentation.physical_multipoint_main`. Definitions checked: `RegularSLEPresentation` (BrownianStrongMarkov.lean:332). The Brownian law is required of `P.comap Subtype.val` on an almost-everywhere-full measurable `samples` set, so the conclusion's measure is the one carrying the Brownian law. An instance is built in RetainedSeedMoments.lean:570, so the structure is not empty. Also checked `IsCapacityTwoWitness`, `survivingDomain`, `upperHalfPlane` and `fullRadius` (LoewnerCharts.lean), `physicalConformalRadius` (MultipointPhysicalGeometry.lean) and `PublishedDiskUnivalentGrowth` (MultipointGeometry.lean:14). `PublishedDiskUnivalentGrowth` is the correct Koebe growth bound and is proved as `actual_diskUnivalentGrowth` (Loewner/ActualDiskGrowth.lean). GaugeGrowthDischarge.lean:39 passes that proof in for `hgrowth`, so taking it as a hypothesis is a deliberate choice, and the assumption is true, not inconsistent. The hypotheses can all be met together (e.g. J = id, distinct points in the upper half-plane, 0 < κ < 8, small positive b and e). The exponent 1-κ/8 is positive, and the `min 1` cap gives the trivial bound when e i ≥ b i. The event lets each point have its own time and requires the point to still be in the surviving domain, which rules out junk values of the radius. `hbR` bounds b i by the conformal radius of J(ℍ) at J(z i), and `hsep` gives the separation. The constant depends only on κ and m, as the module comment says. The theorem matches `Multipoint.capped_physical_radius_multipoint_bound` with ι = Fin m and R i := 2·Im(z i)·‖J'(z i)‖. Remaining uncertainty: I did not open the cited paper, so whether this matches its multipoint proposition rests on the docstrings and definitions. I also did not look inside `uniformDiscountBudget` or `sourceBeta`; their values don't affect vacuity because the constant only has to depend on κ and m.
